title: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine recommendations for adults: a review of available global, regional, and country level recommendations
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) can cause serious disease in older adults (OAs), particularly those with underlying medical conditions. It can lead to acute respiratory illness and lower respiratory tract infections in adults ≥60 years and at increased risk groups. RSV morbidity, mortality, and health care burden are increasingly evident. This review aims to equip clinicians with practical guidance to support consistent implementation of RSV vaccination recommendations. AREAS COVERED: We examined global implementation of RSV vaccination recommendations by extracting guidelines from national immunization technical advisory groups, ministries of health, global and regional recommendations, and local medical societies. We categorized guidance by age, risk factors and comorbidities. We compared differences in indications, age thresholds, and frameworks. Across >24 countries and >50 medical societies, a common recommendation supports RSV vaccination in ≥60 years and immunocompromised individuals. The set cutoff date was November 2025. However, significant heterogeneity exists across countries in age threshold indications and risk-based eligibility, as well as in implementation depending on health system infrastructure and resources. EXPERT OPINION: Global guidance converges on prioritizing vaccination for OAs and individuals at high risk of severe disease. By synthesizing worldwide RSV vaccination recommendations, this review offers clinicians an accessible guide to support consistent RSV vaccination.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines RSV vaccine recommendations for adults globally, focusing on older adults (OAs) and those at increased risk of severe disease. The analysis highlights that RSV can cause serious illness in adults ≥60 years and those with underlying conditions, leading to acute respiratory illness and lower respiratory tract infections. A common recommendation across >24 countries and >50 medical societies supports vaccination for OAs and immunocompromised individuals. Despite this consensus, significant heterogeneity exists in age thresholds, risk-based eligibility, and implementation, influenced by health system infrastructure and resources. The review aims to provide clinicians with practical guidance to ensure consistent application of RSV vaccination recommendations, offering an accessible synthesis of worldwide guidelines.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)可导致老年成人(OAs)严重疾病,尤其是那些有基础疾病的人群。RSV发病率、患病率及医疗负担日益明显。我们将指导分为年龄、风险因素和合并症类别。我们比较了不同国家在适应症、年龄阈值和框架上的差异。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 设定的截止日期为2025年11月。我们通过提取国家免疫技术咨询小组、卫生部、全球及区域推荐意见以及地方医学学会的指南,考察了全球范围内RSV疫苗接种推荐意见的实施情况。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 它可引起≥60岁成人及高风险群体的急性呼吸道疾病和下呼吸道感染。在超过24个国家和超过50个医学学会中,普遍推荐对≥60岁人群和免疫功能低下者进行RSV疫苗接种。全球指导趋于一致,优先为老年成人(OAs)和严重疾病高风险人群推荐RSV疫苗接种。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 然而,各国在年龄阈值适应症和基于风险的资格认定方面存在显著异质性,且在实施过程中也因卫生系统基础设施和资源的不同而有所差异。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 本综述旨在为临床医生提供实用指导,以支持一致实施RSV疫苗接种推荐意见。通过综合全球RSV疫苗接种推荐意见,本综述为临床医生提供了一个易于获取的指南,以支持一致实施RSV疫苗接种。

title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

title: Human Metapneumovirus in the Post-pandemic Era:: A Multicenter Comparative Study With Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Argentina, 2022–2025
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV), identified in 2001, is an important cause of acute lower respiratory infections (ALRI) in children worldwide and is generally considered the second most frequent viral cause after respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Comparative data between hMPV and RSV in the post-pandemic period remain scarce in Latin America, particularly after the introduction of maternal RSV immunization. METHODS: We conducted a prospective multicenter surveillance study in 5 tertiary pediatric hospitals in Argentina between 2022 and 2025. Children hospitalized with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV or RSV-associated ALRI were included. Epidemiologic characteristics, clinical presentation, respiratory support requirements, outcomes and seasonal patterns were compared. Independent predictors of hMPV versus RSV infection were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 19,021 ALRI hospitalizations, 661 (3.5%) were hMPV and 2397 (12.6%) were RSV cases. hMPV patients were older (median 10 vs 8 months; P < 0.001), had more comorbidities (59% vs. 47%; P < 0.001) and had prior respiratory hospitalizations (42% vs. Fever was more frequent in hMPV (74% vs. 65%; P < 0.001), and focal pneumonia predominated over bronchiolitis. RSV required more advanced respiratory support. Mortality was extremely low and comparable. Independent predictors of hMPV included age 6-23 months and prior respiratory hospitalizations; hMPV risk was lower in 2023-2025 versus 2022. hMPV peaked later than RSV. CONCLUSIONS: This emerging respiratory virus demonstrates distinct epidemiologic and clinical characteristics, predominantly affecting older children with respiratory vulnerability. In the era of RSV prevention strategies, hMPV may represent an increasingly important contributor to the residual burden of severe pediatric ALRI, highlighting the need for development of preventive interventions.

analysis.methods: Epidemiologic characteristics, clinical presentation, respiratory support requirements, outcomes and seasonal patterns were compared, and independent predictors of hMPV versus RSV infection were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Among 19,021 ALRI hospitalizations, 661 (3.5%) were hMPV and 2397 (12.6%) were RSV cases. hMPV patients were older (median 10 vs 8 months; P < 0.001), had more comorbidities (59% vs 47%; P < 0.001) and had prior respiratory hospitalizations (42% vs 20%). analysis.summary_en: This study compares human metapneumovirus (hMPV) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the post-pandemic era in Argentina. It highlights that hMPV is a significant cause of acute lower respiratory infections (ALRI) in children, with distinct epidemiologic and clinical features compared to RSV. The findings suggest that hMPV predominantly affects older children with respiratory vulnerability and may contribute to the residual burden of severe pediatric ALRI despite low mortality rates. The study's large sample size and comprehensive analysis provide strong evidence, though its observational design introduces potential limitations.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important cause of acute lower respiratory infections (ALRI) in children worldwide, and comparative data between hMPV and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the post-pandemic period remain scarce in Latin America, particularly after the introduction of maternal RSV immunization.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A prospective multicenter surveillance study was conducted in 5 tertiary pediatric hospitals in Argentina between 2022 and 2025, including children hospitalized with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV or RSV-associated ALRI.
analysis_en.methods: Epidemiologic characteristics, clinical presentation, respiratory support requirements, outcomes and seasonal patterns were compared, and independent predictors of hMPV versus RSV infection were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 19,021 ALRI hospitalizations, 661 (3.5%) were hMPV and 2397 (12.6%) were RSV cases. hMPV patients were older (median 10 vs 8 months; P < 0.001), had more comorbidities (59% vs 47%; P < 0.001) and had prior respiratory hospitalizations (42% vs 20%). Fever was more frequent in hMPV (74% vs 65%; P < 0.001), and focal pneumonia predominated over bronchiolitis. RSV required more advanced respiratory support. Mortality was extremely low and comparable. hMPV peaked later than RSV.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that hMPV demonstrates distinct epidemiologic and clinical characteristics, predominantly affecting older children with respiratory vulnerability.

analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and comprehensive analysis.

title_zh: 后疫情时代的人类副流感病毒:与呼吸道合胞病毒在阿根廷的多中心比较研究,2022–2025
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV), identified in 2001, is an important cause of acute lower respiratory infections (ALRI) in children worldwide and is generally considered the second most frequent viral cause after respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Comparative data between hMPV and RSV in the post-pandemic period remain scarce in Latin America, particularly after the introduction of maternal RSV immunization. METHODS: We conducted a prospective multicenter surveillance study in 5 tertiary pediatric hospitals in Argentina between 2022 and 2025. Children hospitalized with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction-confirmed hMPV or RSV-associated ALRI were included. Epidemiologic characteristics, clinical presentation, respiratory support requirements, outcomes and seasonal patterns were compared. Independent predictors of hMPV versus RSV infection were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 19,021 ALRI hospitalizations, 661 (3.5%) were hMPV and 2397 (12.6%) were RSV cases. hMPV patients were older (median 10 vs 8 months; P < 0.001), had more comorbidities (59% vs. 47%; P < 0.001) and had prior respiratory hospitalizations (42% vs. Fever was more frequent in hMPV (74% vs. 65%; P < 0.001), and focal pneumonia predominated over bronchiolitis. RSV required more advanced respiratory support. Mortality was extremely low and comparable. Independent predictors of hMPV included age 6-23 months and prior respiratory hospitalizations; hMPV risk was lower in 2023-2025 versus 2022. hMPV peaked later than RSV. CONCLUSIONS: This emerging respiratory virus demonstrates distinct epidemiologic and clinical characteristics, predominantly affecting older children with respiratory vulnerability. In the era of RSV prevention strategies, hMPV may represent an increasingly important contributor to the residual burden of severe pediatric ALRI, highlighting the need for development of preventive interventions.
abstract_zh: 背景:人类副流感病毒(hMPV)自2001年被发现以来,已成为全球儿童急性下呼吸道感染(ALRI)的重要病因,通常被认为是仅次于呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的第二常见病毒病因。然而,在疫情后时期,关于hMPV与RSV的比较数据在拉丁美洲仍较为有限,尤其是在引入母体RSV疫苗接种后。方法:我们于2022年至2025年在阿根廷的5家三级儿科医院开展了一项前瞻性多中心研究。纳入了经逆转录酶聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)确认的hMPV或RSV相关ALRI住院儿童。比较了流行病学特征、临床表现、呼吸支持需求、结局及季节性模式。使用多变量逻辑回归分析评估hMPV与RSV感染的独立预测因素。结果:在19,021例ALRI住院病例中,有661例(3.5%)为hMPV感染,2397例(12.6%)为RSV感染。hMPV感染患儿年龄较大(中位数10个月 vs 8个月;P < 0.001),合并症更多(59% vs 47%;P < 0.001),且有更多既往呼吸道住院史(42% vs. 发热在hMPV感染中更为常见(74% vs. 65%;P < 0.001),且以局灶性肺炎为主,而RSV则需要更高级的呼吸支持。hMPV的死亡率极低且与RSV相当。hMPV的独立预测因素包括年龄6-23个月和既往呼吸道住院史;与2022年相比,2023-2025年hMPV的风险较低。hMPV的高峰出现时间晚于RSV。结论:这种新兴的呼吸道病毒表现出独特的流行病学和临床特征,主要影响有呼吸道脆弱性的年长儿童。在RSV预防策略实施的时代,hMPV可能成为严重儿科ALRI残留负担的重要贡献者,凸显了开发预防干预措施的必要性。

title: Incidence and risk factors of acute respiratory illness associated with influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus within a birth cohort study
abstract: UNLABELLED: Influenza virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are leading causes of acute respiratory infections (ARIs). New Zealand's coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) public health measures disrupted the circulation of these viruses in 2020-2021, creating a rare opportunity to explore the impact of potential immunity gaps on age-specific infection risk. We analyzed data from 843 participants aged between 0 and 4 years enrolled in the Southern Hemisphere Influenza and Vaccine Effectiveness Research and Surveillance 3 (SHIVERS-III) birth cohort, a longitudinal community-based study in New Zealand, during 2020-2024. During the respiratory season, weekly surveillance captured ARI symptoms and severity. Nasal swabs were collected from symptomatic participants and tested for viral RNA by RT-PCR. Incidence rates (IRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated for the surveillance period and adjusted for age, sex, ethnic group, socioeconomic status, and influenza vaccination status. No influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infections were detected in 2020 and 2021. From 2021 to 2024, RSV had the highest IR during the surveillance period (63.2/100 person-years [PY]; 95% CI, 56.6-69.8), followed by SARS-CoV-2 (39.3/100 PY; 95% CI, 34.5-44) and influenza (35.7/100 PY; 95% CI, 29-42.3). Age influenced infection risk: infants <6 months had the lowest incidence of influenza and RSV, potentially reflecting maternally derived immunity and limited exposure. Risk increased after 6 months of age, peaking at age 1 year for RSV and at age 2 years for influenza. Influenza vaccination lowered symptomatic influenza risk (IRR 0.66; 95% CI, 0.44-1.00). In the New Zealand community setting in the post-COVID-19 era, individual respiratory virus illness patterns differ in children aged 0-4. Influenza vaccine shows protection, and age influences virus-specific risk. IMPORTANCE: Influenza virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are major causes of acute respiratory illness in early childhood, yet current understanding is largely reliant on hospital-based surveillance that underestimates the broader community burden. This study addresses this limitation by providing comprehensive, community-based estimates of incidence, severity, and symptom profiles across these viruses within a single longitudinal birth cohort. By leveraging the unique epidemiological context created by pandemic-related disruptions, it offers important insights into how changes in exposure influence subsequent infection risk and virus circulation. The direct comparison of three major respiratory viruses within the same population highlights distinct age-related risk patterns and disease characteristics. In addition, our research provides real-world evidence of the reduced risk of influenza-associated acute respiratory illness among vaccinated children. These findings strengthen the evidence base for age-targeted immunization strategies and improve understanding of early-life respiratory virus epidemiology.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the incidence and risk factors of acute respiratory illness associated with influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) within a birth cohort of children aged 0-4 years in New Zealand. The research highlights the impact of pandemic-related disruptions on viral circulation and provides insights into age-specific infection risks. RSV was found to have the highest incidence rate during the surveillance period, followed by SARS-CoV-2 and influenza. The study also demonstrates that influenza vaccination reduces the risk of symptomatic influenza. The findings suggest that age plays a significant role in infection risk, with infants under 6 months showing lower rates due to potential maternal immunity. These results contribute to the understanding of early-life respiratory virus epidemiology and support the development of age-targeted immunization strategies. The evidence is based on community-based surveillance and is considered moderate in strength due to the absence of reported limitations.

title: Human metapneumovirus-associated ARI hospitalisation rates in comparison to respiratory syncytial virus and influenza in eastern China, 2020-2024: a time-series analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: We estimated human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-associated acute respiratory infection (ARI) hospitalisations in eastern China, and provided a direct comparison with RSV and influenza during 2020-2024. METHODS: Leveraging a large regional medical database, we analysed weekly ARI hospitalisations and viral test-positives (hMPV, RSV and influenza) by age group and region, using negative binomial regression models with natural cubic splines, time-offsets for viral activity, excluding COVID-19 patients and adjusting for COVID-19 waves. RESULTS: hMPV, RSV, and influenza were associated with 100,792 (5.35%), 266,826 (14.17%), and 409,599 (21.76%) ARI hospitalisations, respectively. RSV hospitalisations rebounded first in 2021/2022, followed by hMPV in 2022/2023, while influenza hospitalisations increased annually during the study period; meanwhile, hMPV- and influenza-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged 5-19 years, while RSV-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged ≥5 years. hMPV rates were highest among infants aged 0-5 months and 6-11 months (6.19 and 8.15 per 1,000 per year on average, respectively), followed by ages 12-23 months (18.54). RSV and influenza rates were highest in age groups within <1 year and 1-4 years, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Infants aged <1 year are the primary group for preventing severe hMPV infections, with a substantial additional burden observed in children aged 1-4 years. These findings support hMPV vaccine development and virus-specific intervention strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to estimate the hospitalisation rates of human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) in eastern China and compare them directly with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza during 2020-2024.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A time-series analysis was conducted using a large regional medical database, examining weekly ARI hospitalisations and viral test-positives for hMPV, RSV, and influenza by age group and region in eastern China from 2020 to 2024.
analysis.methods: Negative binomial regression models with natural cubic splines and time-offsets for viral activity were used, excluding patients with COVID-19 and adjusting for the impact of COVID-19 waves.
analysis.main_results: hMPV was associated with 100,792 (5.35%) ARI hospitalisations, RSV with 266,826 (14.17%), and influenza with 409,599 (21.76%). RSV hospitalisations rebounded first in 2021/2022, followed by hMPV in 2022/2023, while influenza hospitalisations increased annually. hMPV- and influenza-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged 5-19 years, while RSV-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged ≥5 years.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the distinct age-related patterns of hMPV and RSV hospitalisations, with hMPV showing a higher burden in infants aged 0-5 months and 6-11 months, and RSV and influenza having higher rates in younger age groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical insights for targeted surveillance, diagnosis, and intervention strategies, particularly for infants and young children, to mitigate the burden of hMPV and RSV infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on a regional medical database and excludes patients with COVID-19, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the time-series analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study estimates the hospitalisation rates of human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) in eastern China and compares them with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza during 2020-2024. Using a regional medical database and negative binomial regression models, the analysis excludes patients with COVID-19 and adjusts for its impact. Results show hMPV was associated with 100,792 (5.35%) ARI hospitalisations, RSV with 266,826 (14.17%), and influenza with 409,599 (21.76%). RSV hospitalisations rebounded first in 2021/2022, followed by hMPV in 2022/2023, while influenza hospitalisations increased annually. The findings indicate distinct age-related patterns, with hMPV and influenza affecting older children more, and RSV affecting those aged ≥5 years. The study supports the development of hMPV-specific interventions and highlights the need for targeted public health strategies. However, the reliance on a regional database and exclusion of COVID-19 patients may limit generalisability, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to estimate the hospitalisation rates of human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) in eastern China and compare them directly with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza during 2020-2024.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A time-series analysis was conducted using a large regional medical database, examining weekly ARI hospitalisations and viral test-positives for hMPV, RSV, and influenza by age group and region in eastern China from 2020 to 2024.
elements_en.methods: Negative binomial regression models with natural cubic splines and time-offsets for viral activity were used, excluding patients with COVID-19 and adjusting for the impact of COVID-19 waves.
elements_en.main_results: hMPV was associated with 100,792 (5.35%) ARI hospitalisations, RSV with 266,826 (14.17%), and influenza with 409,599 (21.76%). RSV hospitalisations rebounded first in 2021/2022, followed by hMPV in 2022/2023, while influenza hospitalisations increased annually. hMPV- and influenza-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged 5-19 years, while RSV-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged ≥5 years.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the distinct age-related patterns of hMPV and RSV hospitalisations, with hMPV showing a higher burden in infants aged 0-5 months and 6-11 months, and RSV and influenza having higher rates in younger age groups.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical insights for targeted surveillance, diagnosis, and intervention strategies, particularly for infants and young children, to mitigate the burden of hMPV and RSV infections.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on a regional medical database and excludes patients with COVID-19, which may limit generalisability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the time-series analysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在估测东部中国人偏肺病毒(hMPV)相关急性呼吸道感染(ARI)的住院率,并在2020-2024年间直接与呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和流感进行比较。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 利用一个大型区域医疗数据库,进行了时间序列分析,考察了2020年至2024年间东部中国按年龄组和区域划分的每周ARI住院率和hMPV、RSV、流感的病毒检测阳性情况。
elements_zh.methods: 使用带有自然三次样条曲线和时间偏移量的负二项回归模型分析病毒活动,排除了患有 COVID-19 的患者,并调整了 COVID-19 波浪的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: hMPV与100,792(5.35%)的ARI住院率相关,RSV与266,826(14.17%)相关,流感与409,599(21.76%)相关。RSV住院率在2021/2022年率先反弹,随后是hMPV在2022/2023年,而流感住院率在研究期间每年增加;同时,hMPV和流感相关的住院率向5-19岁年龄组转移,而RSV相关的住院率则向≥5岁年龄组转移。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突出了hMPV和RSV住院率在年龄相关的不同模式,其中hMPV在0-5个月和6-11个月的婴儿中显示出更高的负担,而RSV和流感则在更小的年龄组中具有更高的住院率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为针对监测、诊断以及干预策略提供了关键的见解,特别是针对婴儿和幼儿,以减轻hMPV和RSV感染的负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于区域医疗数据库,并排除了患有 COVID-19 的患者,这可能会限制其普遍适用性。由于是时间序列分析的观察性研究,证据等级为中等。

title_zh: 东部中国2020-2024年间人偏肺病毒相关急性呼吸道感染住院率与呼吸道合胞病毒及流感的比较:一项时间序列分析。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: We estimated human metapneumovirus (hMPV)-associated acute respiratory infection (ARI) hospitalisations in eastern China, and provided a direct comparison with RSV and influenza during 2020-2024. METHODS: Leveraging a large regional medical database, we analysed weekly ARI hospitalisations and viral test-positives (hMPV, RSV and influenza) by age group and region, using negative binomial regression models with natural cubic splines, time-offsets for viral activity, excluding COVID-19 patients and adjusting for COVID-19 waves. RESULTS: hMPV, RSV, and influenza were associated with 100,792 (5.35%), 266,826 (14.17%), and 409,599 (21.76%) ARI hospitalisations, respectively. RSV hospitalisations rebounded first in 2021/2022, followed by hMPV in 2022/2023, while influenza hospitalisations increased annually during the study period; meanwhile, hMPV- and influenza-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged 5-19 years, while RSV-associated hospitalisations shifted towards those aged ≥5 years. hMPV rates were highest among infants aged 0-5 months and 6-11 months (6.19 and 8.15 per 1,000 per year on average, respectively), followed by ages 12-23 months (18.54). RSV and influenza rates were highest in age groups within <1 year and 1-4 years, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Infants aged <1 year are the primary group for preventing severe hMPV infections, with a substantial additional burden observed in children aged 1-4 years. These findings support hMPV vaccine development and virus-specific intervention strategies.

title: Under pressure: lessons learnt from rapid implementation of the respiratory syncytial virus maternal vaccine and infant nirsevimab in Sydney, Australia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to share lessons from the rapid implementation of RSV prevention products and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. The research addresses the need for effective strategies to improve RSV vaccine and nirsevimab adoption in clinical settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved the rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable monoclonal antibody nirsevimab in two maternity hospitals within the Sydney Local Health District. It examined immunisation uptake over a period from February to September 2025.
analysis.methods: Deidentified summary data from electronic medical records were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used to evaluate the rollout process.
analysis.main_results: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in the two hospitals increased from 4% in the first month of rollout to 70-74% from June to September 2025. The number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased as antenatal coverage improved. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reasons for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved during the rollout.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the importance of multidisciplinary engagement and clear messaging in the successful rollout of RSV prevention programs. The study highlights the challenges and strategies for integrating multiple immunisation products into routine clinical practice.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of future RSV prevention programs by emphasizing the need for coordinated efforts, clinician education, and systematic safeguards to ensure accurate implementation. They also provide insights into improving immunisation uptake and documentation in maternity settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on deidentified summary data and the absence of recorded reasons for nirsevimab refusal. The evidence is moderate, as it reflects real-world implementation challenges but lacks deeper causal analysis or control groups.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, including the maternal vaccine and the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab, in two maternity hospitals in Sydney, Australia. It reports that RSV vaccination coverage among mothers improved significantly from 4% in February 2025 to 70-74% by September 2025. The number of infants requiring nirsevimab decreased as maternal coverage increased, while 36% of eligible newborns declined the antibody without recorded reasons. The authors highlight the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration, clinician education, and integrating immunisation into medical workflows for successful program adoption. They note that while the rollout was effective, the study lacks detailed causal analysis and control groups, limiting the strength of the evidence to a moderate level.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在分享快速实施 RSV 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。该研究解决了对有效策略的需求,以改善 RSV 疫苗 和 尼塞韦单抗 在临床环境中的采用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及在悉尼本地卫生区的两家 maternity 医院推广呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)母体疫苗 疫苗 和可注射单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗,考察了 2025 年 2 月至 9 月期间的疫苗接种率。
elements_zh.methods: 从电子病历中提取的匿名汇总数据被描述性分析为计数和比例。采用实施研究综合框架(Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research)评估推广过程。
elements_zh.main_results: 在两家医院分娩的女性中,RSV 母体疫苗 疫苗接种 的接种率从推广首月的 4% 上升到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月期间的 70-74%。随着产前接种率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36% 的家庭拒绝接种 尼塞韦单抗,但拒绝的原因未被记录。在推广过程中,RSV 疫苗接种状态的记录有所改善。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明多学科协作和清晰信息传达在成功推广 RSV 预防计划中的重要性。该研究突出了在常规临床实践中整合多种疫苗产品的挑战和策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为未来 RSV 预防计划的制定提供参考,强调需要协调努力、医务人员教育和系统性保障措施以确保准确实施。它们还提供了改善 maternity 环境中疫苗接种率和记录的见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖匿名汇总数据,且未记录 尼塞韦单抗 拒绝的原因。证据强度中等,因为它反映了实际实施中的挑战,但缺乏更深入的因果分析或对照组。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及在悉尼本地卫生区的两家 maternity 医院推广呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)母体疫苗 疫苗 和可注射单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗,考察了 2025 年 2 月至 9 月期间的疫苗接种率。
analysis_zh.methods: 从电子病历中提取的匿名汇总数据被描述性分析为计数和比例。采用实施研究综合框架(Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research)评估推广过程。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在两家医院分娩的女性中,RSV 母体疫苗 疫苗接种 的接种率从推广首月的 4% 上升到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月期间的 70-74%。随着产前接种率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36% 的家庭拒绝接种 尼塞韦单抗,但拒绝的原因未被记录。在推广过程中,RSV 疫苗接种状态的记录有所改善。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明多学科协作和清晰信息传达在成功推广 RSV 预防计划中的重要性。该研究突出了在常规临床实践中整合多种疫苗产品的挑战和策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为未来 RSV 预防计划的制定提供参考,强调需要协调努力、医务人员教育和系统性保障措施以确保准确实施。它们还提供了改善 maternity 环境中疫苗接种率和记录的见解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖匿名汇总数据,且未记录 尼塞韦单抗 拒绝的原因。证据强度中等,因为它反映了实际实施中的挑战,但缺乏更深入的因果分析或对照组。

title: Bacterial co-infection in patients hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus and influenza a infection: a retrospective observational cohort study
abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the prevalence, microbiological characteristics, and clinical impact of bacterial co-infection in adults hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or influenza A infection. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV or influenza A infection in Central Denmark. Bacterial co-infection was identified using bacterial culturing and urinary antigen testing. Poisson regression was used to estimate risk ratios for bacterial co-infection, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate associations between bacterial co-infection and adverse clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Among 4,537 patients, 1,394 had RSV infection and 3,143 had influenza A infection. Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/611 (30.6%) RSV-infected patients and 298/947 (31.5%) influenza A-infected patients (p = 0.72). Among all patients bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/1,394 (13.4%) RSV infected patients and 298/3,143 (9.5%) influenza A infected patients (p < 0.01) Haemophilus influenzae was the most common pathogen in both groups, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus. Bacterial co-infection was associated with increased ICU admission and mortality among influenza A infected patients, whereas estimates were lower in RSV. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified at similar rates in patients hospitalized with RSV and influenza A infection. The most frequently isolated bacteria in both viral groups were bacterial species harboring genes for beta-lactamase production. These findings support consideration of tailoring the empirical antibiotic therapy to cover pathogens with beta-lactamase production when bacterial co-infection is suspected in RSV and influenza A infected patients. Bacterial co-infection was associated with poorer clinical outcomes in Influenza A than RSV.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the prevalence, microbiological characteristics, and clinical impact of bacterial co-infection in adults hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or influenza A infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted on adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV or influenza A infection in Central Denmark between 2015 and 2023.
analysis.methods: Bacterial co-infection was identified using bacterial culturing and urinary antigen testing. Poisson regression was used to estimate risk ratios for bacterial co-infection, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate associations between bacterial co-infection and adverse clinical outcomes.
analysis.main_results: Among 4,537 patients, 1,394 had RSV infection and 3,143 had influenza A infection. Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/611 (30.6%) RSV-infected patients and 298/947 (31.5%) influenza A-infected patients (p = 0.72). Among all patients, bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/1,394 (13.4%) RSV infected patients and 298/3,143 (9.5%) influenza A infected patients (p < 0.01). Haemophilus influenzae was the most common pathogen in both groups, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that bacterial co-infection occurs at similar rates in patients hospitalized with RSV and influenza A infection, and that Haemophilus influenzae is the most frequently isolated bacteria in both groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that empirical antibiotic therapy should consider covering pathogens with beta-lactamase production when bacterial co-infection is suspected in RSV and influenza A infected patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and use of statistical methods to evaluate associations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated bacterial co-infection in adults hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or influenza A infection. It found that bacterial co-infection occurred at similar rates in both viral groups, with Haemophilus influenzae being the most common pathogen. The results suggest that empirical antibiotic therapy should be tailored to cover beta-lactamase-producing pathogens in these patients. The study's large sample size and statistical methods support its findings, though its retrospective design may introduce bias.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在比较呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)或流感A病毒感染住院成人患者中细菌共感染的流行情况、微生物学特征和临床影响。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the prevalence, microbiological characteristics, and clinical impact of bacterial co-infection in adults hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or influenza A infection.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted on adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV or influenza A infection in Central Denmark between 2015 and 2023.
analysis_en.methods: Bacterial co-infection was identified using bacterial culturing and urinary antigen testing. Poisson regression was used to estimate risk ratios for bacterial co-infection, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate associations between bacterial co-infection and adverse clinical outcomes.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 4,537 patients, 1,394 had RSV infection and 3,143 had influenza A infection. Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/611 (30.6%) RSV-infected patients and 298/947 (31.5%) influenza A-infected patients (p = 0.72). Among all patients, bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/1,394 (13.4%) RSV infected patients and 298/3,143 (9.5%) influenza A infected patients (p < 0.01). Haemophilus influenzae was the most common pathogen in both groups, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings indicate that bacterial co-infection occurs at similar rates in patients hospitalized with RSV and influenza A infection, and that Haemophilus influenzae is the most frequently isolated bacteria in both groups.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that empirical antibiotic therapy should consider covering pathogens with beta-lactamase production when bacterial co-infection is suspected in RSV and influenza A infected patients.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and use of statistical methods to evaluate associations.

title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒和流感A病毒感染住院患者中的细菌共感染:一项回顾性观察性研究
source_body_en: PURPOSE: To compare the prevalence, microbiological characteristics, and clinical impact of bacterial co-infection in adults hospitalized with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) or influenza A infection. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV or influenza A infection in Central Denmark. Bacterial co-infection was identified using bacterial culturing and urinary antigen testing. Poisson regression was used to estimate risk ratios for bacterial co-infection, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate associations between bacterial co-infection and adverse clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Among 4,537 patients, 1,394 had RSV infection and 3,143 had influenza A infection. Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/611 (30.6%) RSV-infected patients and 298/947 (31.5%) influenza A-infected patients (p = 0.72). Among all patients bacterial co-infection was identified in 187/1,394 (13.4%) RSV infected patients and 298/3,143 (9.5%) influenza A infected patients (p < 0.01) Haemophilus influenzae was the most common pathogen in both groups, followed by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus. Bacterial co-infection was associated with increased ICU admission and mortality among influenza A infected patients, whereas estimates were lower in RSV. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing microbiological testing, bacterial co-infection was identified at similar rates in patients hospitalized with RSV and influenza A infection. The most frequently isolated bacteria in both viral groups were bacterial species harboring genes for beta-lactamase production. These findings support consideration of tailoring the empirical antibiotic therapy to cover pathogens with beta-lactamase production when bacterial co-infection is suspected in RSV and influenza A infected patients. Bacterial co-infection was associated with poorer clinical outcomes in Influenza A than RSV.
abstract_zh: 目的:比较呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)或流感A病毒感染住院成人患者中细菌共感染的流行情况、微生物学特征和临床影响。方法:我们对2015年至2023年间中央丹麦地区实验室确诊的RSV或流感A病毒感染住院成人患者进行了回顾性观察性研究。通过细菌培养和尿液抗原检测确定细菌共感染。使用泊松回归估计细菌共感染的风险比,并使用Cox比例风险回归评估细菌共感染与不良临床结局之间的关联。结果:在4,537名患者中,有1,394名感染了RSV,3,143名感染了流感A病毒。在进行微生物学检测的患者中,RSV感染患者中有187/611(30.6%)存在细菌共感染,流感A病毒感染患者中有298/947(31.5%)存在细菌共感染(p = 0.72)。在所有患者中,RSV感染患者中有187/1,394(13.4%)存在细菌共感染,流感A病毒感染患者中有298/3,143(9.5%)存在细菌共感染(p < 0.01)。在两个组中,最常见的病原体是流感嗜血杆菌,其次是肺炎链球菌、卡他莫拉菌和金黄色葡萄球菌。细菌共感染与流感A病毒感染患者的ICU入院和死亡率增加相关,而在RSV感染患者中估计值较低。结论:在进行微生物学检测的患者中,RSV和流感A病毒感染住院患者中细菌共感染的发生率相似。在两种病毒组中,最常见的分离细菌是携带β-内酰胺酶基因的细菌种类。这些发现支持在怀疑RSV和流感A病毒感染患者存在细菌共感染时,应考虑调整经验性抗生素治疗以覆盖携带β-内酰胺酶基因的病原体。细菌共感染与流感A病毒感染患者的临床结局较差相关,而与RSV感染患者的关联较弱。

title: Aspergillus species isolation in respiratory samples from patients with respiratory syncytial virus: An 11-year retrospective single-center cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus is a significant cause of morbidity in adults, but data on fungal coinfections, beyond influenza-associated pulmonary aspergillosis and COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis, remain limited. AIMS: To characterize the isolation of Aspergillus in respiratory samples from adult patients with confirmed respiratory syncytial virus infection over an 11-year period, and to describe associated risk factors, microbiological findings, antifungal treatment, and clinical outcomes. METHODS: We conducted an 11-year retrospective study at Hospital Universitario La Paz (Madrid, Spain) including 17 adult patients with confirmed respiratory syncytial virus infection and Aspergillus isolation from respiratory samples. Episodes were classified as probable invasive aspergillosis or colonization according to clinical, radiological, and microbiological findings. RESULTS: A total of 18 episodes were identified, with the species within the Aspergillus fumigatus complex being the most frequently isolated (78.9%), followed by Aspergillus terreus complex (10.5%), Aspergillus nidulans complex (5.3%), and Aspergillus niger complex (5.3). Most isolates were considered colonization (55.6%), while probable invasive aspergillosis accounted for 44.4% episodes, based on compatible clinical and radiological findings. Corticosteroid exposure was common with 82.4% receiving or starting a corticosteroid therapy during hospitalization, and antifungal therapy was administered in 44.4% of episodes, including voriconazole and liposomal amphotericin B. The median hospital stay was 16 days (IQR: 8-28). Mortality was 11.1%. CONCLUSIONS: Aspergillus isolation in adults with respiratory syncytial virus infection was observed mainly in patients with underlying pulmonary disease or comorbidities, with colonization being more frequent than invasive aspergillosis. However, no episodes of severe invasive aspergillosis requiring intensive care were observed in this cohort. Our study provides novel insights into Aspergillus isolation associated with respiratory syncytial virus infection and emphasizes the need for further multicentric studies to define epidemiology, risk factors, and optimal management strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize the isolation of Aspergillus in respiratory samples from adult patients with confirmed respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection over an 11-year period. Conducted at Hospital Universitario La Paz in Madrid, Spain, it included 17 patients with RSV infection and Aspergillus isolation. The study classified episodes as colonization or probable invasive aspergillosis based on clinical, radiological, and microbiological findings. Results showed that the Aspergillus fumigatus complex was most frequently isolated (78.9%), followed by other species. Colonization was more common than invasive aspergillosis (55.6% vs. 44.4%), with corticosteroid use and antifungal therapy observed in 82.4% and 44.4% of episodes, respectively. The median hospital stay was 16 days, and mortality was 11.1%. The authors concluded that Aspergillus isolation is more prevalent in patients with underlying pulmonary disease or comorbidities, highlighting the need for further research. However, no severe invasive aspergillosis cases requiring intensive care were observed, which may limit the generalizability of findings.

title: Decision-Making About Respiratory Syncytial Virus Immunization for Infants: Qualitative Interview Study
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of infant hospitalization in the United States. Although maternal RSV vaccination and infant RSV monoclonal antibody products are recommended to protect infants during their first RSV season, uptake has remained modest. Understanding how pregnant individuals make decisions about these products is critical for informing strategies that support timely immunization. Objective The study aimed to examine the behavioral and social drivers shaping decisions regarding RSV vaccination during pregnancy and infant RSV monoclonal antibody immunization among pregnant individuals in the United States. Methods We conducted an exploratory qualitative study from a relativist epistemological perspective, using semistructured interviews with 12 pregnant and postpartum adults recruited across the United States between October 2024 and May 2025. Participants were purposively sampled to include individuals with positive, uncertain, and negative intentions toward RSV vaccination. Interviews were guided by the World Health Organization’s behavioral and social drivers of vaccination framework and analyzed using a framework analysis approach. Screening survey data were summarized descriptively to characterize participant immunization intentions and contextualize the qualitative findings. Results RSV immunization decisions reflected interacting behavioral, emotional, social, and practical influences rather than attitudes alone. Participants with positive vaccination intentions described greater trust in medical expertise, confidence in vaccination, and personal or professional experience with RSV illness. Those with unsure or negative intentions emphasized the novelty of RSV vaccines, concerns about safety and long-term effects, and greater reliance on clinician recommendations and peer experiences when making decisions. Across intention groups, participants expressed a preference for receiving protection during pregnancy rather than after birth but reported uncertainty related to vaccine availability, timing within the 32- to 36-week eligibility window, and inconsistent integration into prenatal care. Participants consistently identified trusted clinician communication, opportunities for early discussion, and access to clear educational materials as important influences on decision-making. Conclusions Decisions regarding RSV immunization during pregnancy are shaped by interconnected motivational, interpersonal, and structural factors. Integrating education on RSV and RSV immunization options earlier in prenatal care, strengthening clinician recommendations, and reducing logistical barriers to maternal vaccination may improve informed decision-making and timely uptake of infant RSV protection.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是美国婴儿住院的主要原因。本研究旨在探讨影响美国孕妇在怀孕期间以及婴儿RSV单克隆抗体免疫决策的行为和社会驱动因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 我们从相对主义认识论的角度开展了一项探索性的定性研究,使用半结构化访谈,访谈对象为12名在美国各州招募的孕妇和产后成人,招募时间从2024年10月至2025年5月。访谈基于世界卫生组织的疫苗接种框架的行为和社会驱动因素,并采用框架分析方法进行分析。筛查调查数据被描述性总结,以描述参与者的疫苗接种意图,并为定性发现提供背景。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: RSV免疫决策反映了行为、情感、社会和实际因素的相互作用,而不仅仅是态度。参与者一致认为,值得信赖的临床医生沟通、早期讨论的机会以及获取清晰教育材料的途径是影响决策的重要因素。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 具有不确定或消极意图的参与者强调了RSV 疫苗的新颖性、对安全性和长期影响的担忧,以及在决策过程中更依赖临床医生的建议和同龄人的经验。在所有意图群体中,参与者表达了在怀孕期间接受保护的偏好,而不是出生后,但报告了关于RSV 疫苗供应情况、在32至36周资格窗口内的接种时间以及其在产前护理中整合不一致的不确定性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 在产前护理早期整合RSV及其免疫选项的教育,加强临床医生的建议,并减少母体RSV 疫苗接种的后勤障碍,可能会改善知情决策并促进婴儿RSV保护的及时接种。

title_zh: 关于婴儿呼吸道合胞病毒免疫决策的定性访谈研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of infant hospitalization in the United States. Although maternal RSV vaccination and infant RSV monoclonal antibody products are recommended to protect infants during their first RSV season, uptake has remained modest. Understanding how pregnant individuals make decisions about these products is critical for informing strategies that support timely immunization. Objective The study aimed to examine the behavioral and social drivers shaping decisions regarding RSV vaccination during pregnancy and infant RSV monoclonal antibody immunization among pregnant individuals in the United States. Methods We conducted an exploratory qualitative study from a relativist epistemological perspective, using semistructured interviews with 12 pregnant and postpartum adults recruited across the United States between October 2024 and May 2025. Participants were purposively sampled to include individuals with positive, uncertain, and negative intentions toward RSV vaccination. Interviews were guided by the World Health Organization’s behavioral and social drivers of vaccination framework and analyzed using a framework analysis approach. Screening survey data were summarized descriptively to characterize participant immunization intentions and contextualize the qualitative findings. Results RSV immunization decisions reflected interacting behavioral, emotional, social, and practical influences rather than attitudes alone. Participants with positive vaccination intentions described greater trust in medical expertise, confidence in vaccination, and personal or professional experience with RSV illness. Those with unsure or negative intentions emphasized the novelty of RSV vaccines, concerns about safety and long-term effects, and greater reliance on clinician recommendations and peer experiences when making decisions. Across intention groups, participants expressed a preference for receiving protection during pregnancy rather than after birth but reported uncertainty related to vaccine availability, timing within the 32- to 36-week eligibility window, and inconsistent integration into prenatal care. Participants consistently identified trusted clinician communication, opportunities for early discussion, and access to clear educational materials as important influences on decision-making. Conclusions Decisions regarding RSV immunization during pregnancy are shaped by interconnected motivational, interpersonal, and structural factors. Integrating education on RSV and RSV immunization options earlier in prenatal care, strengthening clinician recommendations, and reducing logistical barriers to maternal vaccination may improve informed decision-making and timely uptake of infant RSV protection.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是美国婴儿住院的主要原因。尽管推荐孕妇使用RSV疫苗和婴儿RSV单克隆抗体产品以保护婴儿在首次RSV季节期间免受感染,但接种率一直保持在较低水平。了解孕妇在这些产品上的决策过程对于制定支持及时免疫策略至关重要。目的 本研究旨在探讨影响美国孕妇在怀孕期间以及婴儿RSV单克隆抗体免疫决策的行为和社会驱动因素。方法 我们从相对主义认识论的角度出发,开展了一项探索性的定性研究,通过半结构化访谈收集了12名来自美国不同地区的孕妇和产后成年人的数据,访谈时间从2024年10月至2025年5月。参与者根据其对RSV疫苗的积极、不确定和消极意向进行目的性抽样。访谈基于世界卫生组织关于RSV疫苗的行为和社会驱动因素框架进行指导,并采用框架分析方法进行分析。筛查调查数据被描述性总结,以表征参与者的免疫意向并为定性发现提供背景。结果 RSV免疫决策反映了行为、情感、社会和实际因素的相互作用,而不仅仅是态度本身。具有积极意向的参与者描述了对医疗专业知识更大的信任、对RSV疫苗的信心以及个人或职业经历中与RSV疾病相关的经验。那些具有不确定或消极意向的参与者则强调了RSV疫苗的新颖性、对其安全性和长期影响的担忧,以及在决策过程中更依赖于医生的建议和同龄人的经验。在所有意向组中,参与者普遍更倾向于在怀孕期间接受保护,而不是在出生后,但报告了关于RSV疫苗供应、在32至36周内接种时间窗口的安排以及其在产前护理中整合不一致的不确定性。参与者一致认为,值得信赖的医生沟通、早期讨论的机会以及获取清晰教育材料的途径是影响决策的重要因素。结论 怀孕期间的RSV免疫决策受到相互关联的动机、人际和结构性因素的影响。在产前护理早期整合RSV及其免疫选项的教育内容、加强医生的建议以及减少孕妇接种RSV疫苗的后勤障碍,可能有助于改善知情决策和及时的婴儿RSV保护接种率。

title: Binding antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus and association with age-specific neutralizing antibodies and hospitalization patterns in Israel
abstract: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) imposes a substantial health burden, particularly in infants and older adults, but comprehensive population-level data describing age-specific antibody responses alongside hospitalization patterns are scarce. To assess RSV seropositivity across demographic and geographic variables, to evaluate age-specific binding and neutralizing antibody responses, and to describe the age distribution of RSV-positive hospitalizations in an independent hospitalized cohort; any comparisons between the serosurvey and the hospitalized cohort are descriptive and hypothesis‐generating. A cross-sectional sero-survey of 1,396 sera samples was conducted to measure RSV binding antibodies using ELISA (values were defined as high-positive, borderline or low-positive). Of them, neutralizing antibodies were assessed in 243 age-stratified sera. An independent cohort of 1,232 RSV-positive hospitalized patients collected during the 2022–2025 winter seasons at a single center was used to evaluate age-specific hospitalization distributions; the two datasets were not linked at the individual level. Overall, the RSV high-seropositivity rate was 7.8%, with infants aged 0–12 months showing the lowest seroprevalence (0.0%) while children aged 13–59 months (15.4%) and adults aged ≥ 60 years (12.9%) showed the highest. RSV geometric mean titers (GMTs) differed significantly by age, increasing from infancy to adulthood and peaking in those aged ≥ 60 years ( p < 0.0001). Higher GMTs were observed among individuals born outside Israel and varied significantly by district, with the highest levels in the South and lowest in Tel Aviv. Among the hospitalized cohort, infants accounted for the largest proportion of RSV-positive hospitalizations (35.3%), followed by adults aged ≥ 60 years (25.4%). These age‐specific patterns are reported for independent datasets and any juxtaposition is descriptive. Neutralizing antibody analysis in 243 age-stratified sera demonstrated strong correlations between binding and neutralizing antibodies in infants and young children, but weak to moderate correlations in older age groups. Age-specific differences in both the quantity and functional quality of antibodies were observed, with marked demographic variation. Because the serosurvey and hospitalized cohort are independent, the observed concordance or discordance between antibody patterns and hospitalization distribution is descriptive and does not establish causality. Whether these patterns relate to RSV susceptibility or hospitalization risk warrants further investigation in prospective studies with individual-level data. These findings highlight the need for targeted vaccination and prevention strategies, particularly for high-risk groups such as infants and older adults.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒)对健康造成显著负担,尤其是在婴儿和老年人中,但描述年龄特异性抗体反应与住院模式的全面人口水平数据仍然稀缺。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 为了评估RSV在不同人口统计学和地理变量中的血清阳性率,评估年龄特异性结合和中和抗体反应,并描述RSV阳性住院病例的年龄分布,我们使用了一个独立的住院队列研究数据集;任何血清调查与住院队列研究之间的比较都是描述性的和假设生成的。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了一项横断面血清学调查,共收集了1,396份血清样本,通过ELISA检测RSV结合抗体(值被定义为高阳性、临界或低阳性)。其中,对243份按年龄分层的血清样本进行了中和抗体评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体而言,RSV高血清阳性率为7.8%,其中0–12个月的婴儿显示出最低的血清流行率(0.0%),而13–59个月的儿童(15.4%)和≥60岁的成年人(12.9%)则显示出最高水平。RSV几何平均滴度(GMTs)在不同年龄组间存在显著差异,从婴儿期到成年期逐渐上升,并在≥60岁的人群中达到峰值(p < 0.0001)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在抗体的数量和功能质量方面观察到了年龄特异性差异,并且存在显著的人口统计学差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了针对高风险群体(如婴儿和老年人)制定特定疫苗接种和预防策略的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于血清调查和住院队列研究是独立的,因此观察到的抗体模式与住院分布之间的符合或不符合仅是描述性的,不能建立因果关系。

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒)对健康造成显著负担,尤其是在婴儿和老年人中,但描述年龄特异性抗体反应与住院模式的全面人口水平数据仍然稀缺。为了评估RSV在不同人口统计学和地理变量中的血清阳性率,评估年龄特异性结合和中和抗体反应,并描述RSV阳性住院病例的年龄分布,我们使用了一个独立的住院队列研究数据集;任何血清调查与住院队列研究之间的比较都是描述性的和假设生成的。进行了一项横断面血清学调查,共收集了1,396份血清样本,通过ELISA检测RSV结合抗体(值被定义为高阳性、临界或低阳性)。其中,对243份按年龄分层的血清样本进行了中和抗体评估。在2022–2025年冬季,于单一中心收集了1,232份RSV阳性住院患者的独立队列研究数据集,用于评估年龄特异性住院分布;这两个数据集在个体层面未进行关联。总体而言,RSV高血清阳性率为7.8%,其中0–12个月的婴儿显示出最低的血清流行率(0.0%),而13–59个月的儿童(15.4%)和≥60岁的成年人(12.9%)则显示出最高水平。RSV几何平均滴度(GMTs)在不同年龄组间存在显著差异,从婴儿期到成年期逐渐上升,并在≥60岁的人群中达到峰值(p < 0.0001)。在非以色列出生的个体中观察到更高的GMTs,且GMTs在不同地区间存在显著差异,南部地区最高,特拉维夫地区最低。在住院队列研究中,婴儿占RSV阳性住院病例的最大比例(35.3%),其次是≥60岁的成年人(25.4%)。这些年龄特异性模式是在独立数据集中报告的,任何对比都是描述性的。在243份按年龄分层的血清样本中进行的中和抗体分析显示,在婴儿和幼儿中结合抗体与中和抗体之间存在强相关性,但在老年人群中相关性较弱或中等。在抗体的数量和功能质量方面观察到了年龄特异性差异,并且存在显著的人口统计学差异。由于血清调查和住院队列研究是独立的,因此观察到的抗体模式与住院分布之间的符合或不符合仅是描述性的,不能建立因果关系。这些模式是否与RSV易感性或住院风险相关,需要在具有个体层面数据的前瞻性研究中进一步探讨。这些发现强调了针对高风险群体(如婴儿和老年人)制定特定疫苗接种和预防策略的必要性。

title: Subconjunctival Hemorrhage and Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in an Infant Evaluated for Non-accidental Trauma: A Case Report of a Possible Association
abstract: A six-week-old previously healthy infant was found to have a subconjunctival hemorrhage (SCH) and concomitant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection.Because SCH in an infant may represent a sentinel finding of non-accidental trauma (NAT), an extensive multidisciplinary evaluation was performed, which identified no traumatic injuries or evidence of abuse.The SCH resolved within one week, and the patient recovered with supportive care without complications.To our knowledge, SCH in association with RSV has not previously been reported, despite RSV being common in infants.As with SCH reported in association with other respiratory infections, inflammatory and pressure-related processes are possible mechanisms, although this observational case cannot establish causation.Reporting this possible association may broaden the differential diagnosis of SCH to include other medical causes in infants with RSV, while reinforcing the need for completing a thorough screening for abuse.Identifying medical causes for childhood injuries is as important as accurately diagnosing inflicted injury, as misdiagnosing child abuse can have serious medicolegal consequences for children and their families.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the potential association between subconjunctival hemorrhage (SCH) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in an infant, as SCH may be a sentinel finding for non-accidental trauma (NAT).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case report was conducted on a six-week-old infant with a subconjunctival hemorrhage and concomitant RSV infection, evaluated for possible non-accidental trauma.
analysis.methods: An extensive multidisciplinary evaluation was performed to assess for traumatic injuries or evidence of abuse, including clinical examination and diagnostic testing for RSV infection.
analysis.main_results: The infant had a subconjunctival hemorrhage and RSV infection, but no traumatic injuries or evidence of abuse were found. The SCH resolved within one week, and the patient recovered with supportive care without complications.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors suggest that while inflammatory and pressure-related processes may explain the association between SCH and RSV, this observational case cannot establish causation. This case report highlights a possible association that has not been previously documented.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the differential diagnosis of SCH in infants with RSV, emphasizing the importance of considering medical causes alongside potential inflicted injuries.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational nature and lack of control groups, which prevents establishing causation. The evidence is considered moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a six-week-old infant with subconjunctival hemorrhage (SCH) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection who was evaluated for non-accidental trauma. Despite the presence of SCH, which can be a sentinel finding for abuse, no traumatic injuries or evidence of abuse were identified. The SCH resolved within a week, and the infant recovered with supportive care. The authors note that this is the first reported association between SCH and RSV, suggesting possible mechanisms such as inflammation or pressure-related processes, although causation cannot be established. The case underscores the importance of considering medical causes for childhood injuries and highlights the need for thorough screening for abuse in infants with RSV. The study's limitations include its observational design and lack of control groups, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨结膜下出血(SCH)与呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染在婴儿中的潜在关联,因为SCH可能是非意外创伤(NAT)的警示征象。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一名六周大的婴儿进行了病例报告,该婴儿患有结膜下出血和同时发生的RSV感染,并被评估是否存在非意外创伤。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了全面的多学科评估,以检查是否存在创伤性损伤或虐待证据,包括临床检查和RSV感染的诊断测试。
elements_zh.main_results: 该婴儿患有结膜下出血和RSV感染,但未发现创伤性损伤或虐待证据。结膜下出血在一周内消退,患者在接受支持性治疗后无并发症康复。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,尽管炎症和压力相关的机制可能解释结膜下出血与RSV的关联,但这项观察性病例无法确立因果关系。该病例报告突出了一个尚未有文献记载的可能关联。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于扩大对RSV感染婴儿的结膜下出血的鉴别诊断,强调在考虑潜在故意伤害的同时,也要考虑医学原因的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究的观察性质和缺乏对照组,该研究无法确立因果关系。由于这些限制,证据被认为是中等强度的。

abstract_zh: 一名六周大的既往健康的婴儿被发现患有结膜下出血(SCH)和同时发生的呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染。由于婴儿的结膜下出血可能代表非意外创伤(NAT)的警示征象,因此进行了全面的多学科评估,未发现创伤性损伤或虐待证据。结膜下出血在一周内消退,患者在接受支持性治疗后无并发症康复。据我们所知,结膜下出血与RSV的关联尚未有报道,尽管RSV在婴儿中很常见。与结膜下出血与其他呼吸道感染的报道类似,炎症和压力相关的机制可能是解释这种关联的原因,尽管这项观察性病例无法确立因果关系。报告这种可能的关联可能有助于扩大婴儿RSV感染相关结膜下出血的鉴别诊断范围,同时强调对虐待进行彻底筛查的重要性。识别儿童伤害的医学原因与准确诊断故意伤害同样重要,因为误诊儿童虐待可能对儿童及其家庭产生严重的医法后果。
summary_zh: 一名六周大的既往健康的婴儿被发现患有结膜下出血(SCH)和同时发生的呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染。由于婴儿的结膜下出血可能代表非意外创伤(NAT)的警示征象,因此进行了全面的多学科评估,未发现创伤性损伤或虐待证据。结膜下出血在一周内消退,患者在接受支持性治疗后无并发症康复。据我们所知,结膜下出血与RSV的关联尚未有报道,尽管RSV在婴儿中很常见。与结膜下出血与其他呼吸道感染的报道类似,炎症和压力相关的机制可能是解释这种关联的原因,尽管这项观察性病例无法确立因果关系。报告这种可能的关联可能有助于扩大婴儿RSV感染相关结膜下出血的鉴别诊断范围,同时强调对虐待进行彻底筛查的重要性。识别儿童伤害的医学原因与准确诊断故意伤害同样重要,因为误诊儿童虐待可能对儿童及其家庭产生严重的医法后果。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨结膜下出血(SCH)与呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染在婴儿中的潜在关联,因为SCH可能是非意外创伤(NAT)的警示征象。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一名六周大的婴儿进行了病例报告,该婴儿患有结膜下出血和同时发生的RSV感染,并被评估是否存在非意外创伤。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了全面的多学科评估,以检查是否存在创伤性损伤或虐待证据,包括临床检查和RSV感染的诊断测试。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该婴儿患有结膜下出血和RSV感染,但未发现创伤性损伤或虐待证据。结膜下出血在一周内消退,患者在接受支持性治疗后无并发症康复。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,尽管炎症和压力相关的机制可能解释结膜下出血与RSV的关联,但这项观察性病例无法确立因果关系。该病例报告突出了一个尚未有文献记载的可能关联。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于扩大对RSV感染婴儿的结膜下出血的鉴别诊断,强调在考虑潜在故意伤害的同时,也要考虑医学原因的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于研究的观察性质和缺乏对照组,该研究无法确立因果关系。由于这些限制,证据被认为是中等强度的。

title: 06 | Nirsevimab as a key strategy to prevent respiratory syncytial virus among newborns and children: real-world evidence from Italy and Sicily
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the leading causes of lower respiratory tract infections and hospitalization during the first year of life. The introduction of the next-generation long-acting monoclonal antibody Nirsevimab across the Italian Regions, starting from the 2024/25 season, has substantially changed RSV prevention. Administered as a single dose, Nirsevimab has extended protection to all infants during their first RSV season, thereby overcoming the main limitations associated with Palivizumab. Materials and Methods. A non-systematic review of the scientific literature was conducted, focusing on real-world effectiveness (RWE) studies carried out in Italy following the introduction of Nirsevimab during the 2024/2025 season. The main outcomes analyzed included hospitalizations, disease severity, and admissions to intensive care units (ICUs). Real-world effectiveness data available in the scientific literature from different Italian regions have confirmed the high effectiveness of Nirsevimab observed in clinical trials, in line with findings reported in the international literature. A recent meta-analysis of 27 studies conducted in Europe and the United States estimated an 83% reduction in hospitalizations, an 81% reduction in intensive care unit admissions, and a 75% reduction in the incidence of RSV lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs). Studies conducted in Italy have reported immunization effectiveness in real-world settings exceeding 85% in preventing severe RSV disease, over 80% in preventing RSV-related hospitalizations in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) or pediatric wards, and over 70% in preventing emergency department visits for RSV-related illness. Studies based on Italian and Sicilian Hospital Discharge Records have also shown that RSV-related hospitalizations were more than halved during the first season of monoclonal antibody use across different Italian regions, including Sicily. The Italian experience suggests that Nirsevimab represents a paradigm shift in the natural history of RSV disease, with a substantial impact on both the hospital and community healthcare burden. The effectiveness of Nirsevimab can translate into a meaningful public health benefit only if high immunization coverage is achieved, ensuring protection for both in-season and out-of-season births, the latter currently representing a key challenge, with lower uptake rates. It is also important to document informed parental refusal among those who decline prophylaxis and to ensure re-immunization during the second RSV season for vulnerable children (i.e., the former palivizumab-eligible cohort). Furthermore, RespivirNet surveillance data should guide the definition of the immunization window on an annual basis, including consideration of a possible extension of immunization at birth through April 30, in view of the progressively later onset of RSV circulation at both the community and hospital levels, particularly in Southern Italian regions. In summary, nirsevimab represents not merely a new preventive strategy, but a paradigm shift: a true revolution in RSV prevention. The project is part of the Italian Complementary National Plan PNC-I.1 ”Research initiatives for innovative technologies and pathways in the health and welfare sector” D.D. 931 of 06/06/2022, ”DARE - DigitAl lifelong pRevEn-tion” initiative, “Digivax” Pilot Project - code PNC0000002, CUP: B53C22006460001.

title: A ciliated epithelial cell line as a model for respiratory syncytial virus research
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of severe respiratory infection in infants and an increasingly recognized pathogen in the elderly. Conventional in vitro culture models for RSV rely on poorly differentiated cell lines that lack key airway epithelial features such as polarization, tight junctions and cilia, despite ciliated cells being the main RSV target. Primary airway epithelial cultures better reflect in vivo conditions, but they are difficult to access. We evaluated the human bronchial epithelial cell line BCi-NS1.1 differentiated at an air-liquid interface (ALI) as an alternative model. Three weeks after ALI, BCi-NS1.1 cultures exhibited advanced differentiation, including mature tight junctions, IL-13-induced MUC5AC production, a transepithelial potential difference of around −20 mV and 19% ciliated cells. These cultures expressed CX3CR1 receptor in cilia, which may serve as an entry point for RSV. These cultures were readily infected by RSV from the apical side, with infected cell numbers increasing from day 1 to day 5 post-infection. Apical viral titres reached ~2×10 5 PFU ml −1 between day 2 and day 4. Infection led to the formation of typical viral factories with inclusion-body-associated granules, apical release of new infectious virions and controlled shedding of infected cells. Because shedding limits subcellular analysis, we generated an RSV lacking NS2, a protein promoting cell rounding and shedding. Cells infected with RSV-Delta NS2 exhibited slower shedding and maintained their shape longer, enabling visualization of ribonucleoprotein migration towards and across the apical membrane. Overall, ALI-differentiated BCi-NS1.1 cells provide a suitable tool for studying epithelial responses to RSV infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of severe respiratory infection in infants and an increasingly recognized pathogen in the elderly. The study aimed to address the need for a more accurate in vitro model to study RSV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the human bronchial epithelial cell line BCi-NS1.1 differentiated at an air-liquid interface (ALI) as an alternative model for RSV research. The cell line was used to simulate in vivo conditions for studying RSV infection.
analysis.methods: The researchers differentiated the BCi-NS1.1 cell line at an air-liquid interface (ALI) and assessed its characteristics. They also generated an RSV lacking NS2, a protein promoting cell rounding and shedding, to facilitate subcellular analysis.
analysis.main_results: Three weeks after ALI differentiation, BCi-NS1.1 cultures exhibited mature tight junctions, IL-13-induced MUC5AC production, a transepithelial potential difference of around −20 mV and 19% ciliated cells. These cultures were readily infected by RSV from the apical side, with infected cell numbers increasing from day 1 to day 5 post-infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that ALI-differentiated BCi-NS1.1 cells provide a suitable tool for studying epithelial responses to RSV infection, as they closely mimic in vivo conditions and support RSV replication and shedding.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that BCi-NS1.1 cells differentiated at ALI can be used for studying RSV infection mechanisms, which may inform future research on diagnosis, treatment and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro observations and does not account for in vivo complexities. However, the evidence is strong as it directly reports on the characteristics and infection dynamics of RSV in a relevant cell model.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces the human bronchial epithelial cell line BCi-NS1.1 differentiated at an air-liquid interface (ALI) as a potential in vitro model for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) research. RSV is a major cause of severe respiratory infections in infants and the elderly, and conventional cell lines lack key airway epithelial features. The ALI-differentiated BCi-NS1.1 cells showed advanced differentiation, including mature tight junctions, ciliated cells, and a transepithelial potential difference. These cells were infected by RSV from the apical side, with infected cell numbers increasing over days. The study also generated an RSV lacking NS2 to better observe subcellular processes. The authors concluded that these cells provide a suitable tool for studying RSV infection, as they closely mimic in vivo conditions. The findings are significant for future research on RSV mechanisms but are limited to in vitro observations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是婴儿严重呼吸道感染的主要原因,并且在老年人中逐渐被认可为一种病原体。本研究旨在解决对更准确的RSV感染体外模型的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究评估了在气液界面(ALI)分化的人支气管上皮细胞系BCi-NS1.1作为RSV研究的替代模型。该细胞系被用于模拟体内环境以研究RSV感染。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,ALI分化的BCi-NS1.1细胞为研究RSV感染对上皮反应提供了合适的工具,因为它们密切模拟了体内环境,并支持RSV的复制和脱落。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,ALI分化的BCi-NS1.1细胞可用于研究RSV感染机制,这可能为未来关于诊断、治疗以及预防策略的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外观察,未考虑体内复杂性。然而,证据较强,因为它直接报告了RSV在相关细胞模型中的特性及其感染动态。

abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是婴儿严重呼吸道感染的主要原因,并且在老年人中逐渐被认可为一种病原体。尽管纤毛细胞是RSV的主要靶标,但传统的RSV体外培养模型依赖于分化不良的细胞系,这些细胞系缺乏极化、紧密连接和纤毛等关键气道上皮特征。原代气道上皮培养更贴近体内环境,但获取较为困难。本研究评估了在气液界面(ALI)分化的人支气管上皮细胞系BCi-NS1.1作为RSV研究的替代模型。在ALI分化三周后,BCi-NS1.1培养物表现出高级分化特征,包括成熟的紧密连接、IL-13诱导的MUC5AC产生、约−20 mV的跨上皮电位差以及19%的纤毛细胞比例。这些培养物在纤毛上表达CX3CR1受体,这可能为RSV的入侵提供途径。RSV可以从顶端感染这些培养物,感染细胞数量在感染后第1天至第5天持续增加。感染后第2至第4天,顶端病毒滴度达到约2×10^5 PFU ml^{-1}。感染导致形成典型的病毒工厂,包括与包涵体相关的颗粒、顶端释放新的感染性病毒颗粒以及受感染细胞的受控脱落。由于脱落限制了亚细胞分析,我们生成了一种缺乏NS2蛋白(该蛋白促进细胞圆化和脱落)的RSV,以促进亚细胞分析。感染RSV-Delta NS2的细胞表现出较慢的脱落,并且在更长时间内保持其形态,从而能够观察到核糖核蛋白向顶端膜迁移的现象。总体而言,ALI分化的BCi-NS1.1细胞为研究RSV感染对上皮反应提供了合适的工具。

analysis_zh.main_results: 在ALI分化三周后,BCi-NS1.1培养物表现出成熟的紧密连接、IL-13诱导的MUC5AC产生、约−20 mV的跨上皮电位差以及19%的纤毛细胞比例。这些培养物可以从顶端被RSV感染,感染细胞数量在感染后第1天至第5天持续增加。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,ALI分化的BCi-NS1.1细胞为研究RSV感染对上皮反应提供了合适的工具,因为它们密切模拟了体内环境,并支持RSV的复制和脱落。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,ALI分化的BCi-NS1.1细胞可用于研究RSV感染机制,这可能为未来关于诊断、治疗以及预防策略的研究提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外观察,未考虑体内复杂性。然而,证据较强,因为它直接报告了RSV在相关细胞模型中的特性及其感染动态。

title: 01 | Integrated prevention of respiratory syncytial virus in infants after the “revolution”: reflections from the first two seasons in Sicily and Calabria
abstract: The introduction of maternal immunization and monoclonal antibody prophylaxis has substantially changed the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease in infants. After two seasons of implementation, the experience of Sicily and Calabria offers an opportunity to discuss the clinical impact of these strategies and the organisational challenges involved in their delivery. Materials and Methods. This narrative contribution is based on a structured discussion with two healthcare professionals involved in RSV prevention. The first perspective concerns the paediatric impact of the new strategies, including changes in hospital admissions, disease severity and the characteristics of infants who continue to require hospital care. The second focuses on maternal immunization, with particular reference to acceptance among pregnant women, communication needs and the integration of vaccination into birth pathways. The first two seasons suggest a substantial reduction in the burden of severe RSV disease. In Sicily, during the 2024–2025 season, more than 65% of the target population received preventive protection and hospitalizations for RSV bronchiolitis decreased by approximately 40%. However, residual hospitalizations continue to occur, particularly among infants who did not receive timely prophylaxis, very young infants and children with underlying vulnerability. From the perspective of maternal immunization, the main challenges concern the timely identification of eligible women, the coordination between maternity units and vaccination services, and the consistency of information provided by healthcare professionals. Acceptance may be influenced by organisational barriers as well as by communication and cultural factors. The experience of the first two seasons indicates that the effectiveness of RSV prevention depends not only on the availability of maternal immunization and monoclonal antibody prophylaxis, but also on the ability to integrate these interventions into routine care pathways. Strengthening collaboration among maternity units, vaccination services, paediatricians and community healthcare professionals will be essential to improve timely access, reduce residual preventable disease and ensure equitable protection for infants in Sicily and Calabria.
