full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory illness and severe outcomes in older adults. Objective This retrospective cohort study investigated the health and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among adults ≥ 60 years in Japan. Methods Data were collected between 1 September 2008 and 31 August 2021 from the Medical Data Vision (MDV) hospital-based claims database and the insurance-based JMDC database. We investigated RSV-related complications during the first episode. Healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs were compared between baseline (pre-event: 30-day average costs during the 365 days before RSV diagnosis) and post-event (30 days after RSV diagnosis); differences were explored using paired sample t-tests (p < 0.05). Results A total of 178 cases identified between 2009 and 2019 were included in the study, 144 were from the MDV database (mean age 74 years) and 34 from the JMDC database (mean age 64 years). RSV-related complications were recorded in 61.1% and 55.9% of the MDV and JMDC cohorts, respectively. HCRU in the MDV cohort increased significantly from pre- to post-event (average number of outpatient visits per case: 1.21 to 2.07; average number of hospitalizations per case: 0.07 to 0.37), resulting in significant additional medical costs of ¥196,231 (p < 0.001). Conclusions Medically attended RSV infections were associated with substantial short-term increases in HCRU and total medical costs among older adults in Japan. These findings may help inform prevention strategies for severe RSV disease. | Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was associated with substantial short-term increases in healthcare resource utilization and medical costs among medically attended older adults in Japan, particularly during the first 30 days following diagnosis. | | These findings may help inform RSV prevention strategies, including vaccination. | 1 Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common virus affecting individuals of all ages, the most vulnerable being young children and older adults [1]. RSV can lead to severe infections such as pneumonia in older adults, especially those with chronic cardiovascular disease, pulmonary conditions, or diabetes [1,2,3]. Severe RSV infections may require hospitalization or non-invasive ventilation [1]. RSV is associated with lower and upper respiratory tract disease (LRTD/URTD), potentially leading to inflammatory responses that can cause complications such as exacerbation of asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and heart failure [2]. In Japan, the incidence and disease burden of RSV in older adults is likely underestimated due to the lack of routine testing and surveillance. A prospective study estimated that RSV infection occurs in 2.4% of ambulatory older adults in Japan [4]. A recent meta-analysis using 1999–2020 data from high-income countries estimated approximately 700,000 RSV-related acute respiratory infection (ARI) cases, 63,000 hospitalizations, and 4500 in-hospital deaths annually in older adults in Japan [5]. The economic burden of RSV in older adults in Japan is not well documented, but the costs of hospitalization due to RSV contribute considerably to this burden [6]. In 2023, RSV vaccines were approved for individuals aged ≥ 60 years in the USA, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and Japan [7,8,9]. In Japan, the indication was subsequently expanded to include adults aged 50–59 years in 2024 and 18–49 years in 2026, if they were diagnosed with a medical condition that put them at increased risk for severe RSV, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma.[10]. However, there are currently no specific treatments, highlighting a considerable unmet medical need and the importance of vaccination, especially given the high proportion of Japan’s population that is aged > 65 years (30% in 2022) [11]. Understanding the real-world impact of RSV is essential. Estimating its clinical and economic consequences is key to informing optimal vaccination strategies. We conducted a retrospective analysis using data from two administrative claims databases to explore the disease and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among older adults in Japan. 2 Materials and Methods 2.1 Study Design In this retrospective observational cohort study, we investigated the health and economic burden associated with RSV infection among older adults (≥ 60 years) in Japan from 1 September 2008 to 31 August 2021 (Supplementary Fig. 1). Data from two commercially available administrative databases ensured diverse population coverage: a hospital-based database (Medical Data Vision Co. Ltd. [MDV]; Tokyo, Japan) and an insurance-based database (JMDC Inc. Payer). The MDV is an anonymized health claims database including Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination data covering lump-sum payments for acute-care hospital inpatient costs; as of data analysis, it comprises data for approximately 45 million patients and 35% of the data are from cases aged more than 65 years [12]. The JMDC is an anonymized employer-based health insurance claims database with more than 130 payers, covering inpatient, outpatient, and medication-dispensing services, in addition to annual health-check results; as of data analysis, it stores data of 12 million patients among which 2% are aged 65–74 years [13]. The study complied with all applicable privacy laws. It was out of scope of the Ethical Guidelines for Life Sciences and Medical Research Involving Human Subjects in Japan. We assessed identification periods, which were 1-year cycles (September to August), between 2009 and 2020, accounting for the 12-month baseline and follow-up periods (Supplementary Fig. 1). An index event was defined as the first eligible claim with a diagnostic code for RSV within each 1-year cycle. 2.2 Cases and Case Definitions RSV cases were defined as those having at least one RSV diagnosis claim, based on the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision (ICD-10 codes: B34.8 [RSV infection only], J12.1, J20.5, or J21.0) [6, 14], during the identification period. The first RSV diagnosis within each 1-year cycle was included from the MDV (aged ≥ 60 years) or JMDC (aged 60–74 years) at the time of the index event. Cases with associated LRTD/URTD were defined, based on the relevant ICD-10 codes (URTD: B34.8, J00, J01.0–J01.4, J01.9, J02.0, J02.8–J03.0, J03.8–J04.2, J05.0, J05.1, J06.0, J06.8, J06.9, J30.0–J30.4, J34.0–J34.3, J34.8, J36, J38.0, J38.3, J38.4, J38.7, J39.0–J39.2, J39.8; LRTD: J11.0, J12.0, J12.1, J12.2, J12.3, J12.8, J12.9, J13, J14, J15.0–J16.0, J18.0–J18.2, J18.8, J18.9, J20.0–J21.1, J21.9, J22, J40, J44.0, J44.1, J68.0, J69.0, J69.1, J69.8, J70.2, J98.0, J98.2). The index date for RSV cases was derived using database-specific algorithms incorporating available information such as treatment start or hospital admission dates, claim month/year, and inpatient/outpatient service dates recorded in the same month to estimate the diagnosis date. Prediagnosis healthcare seeking was captured one week prior to the index date, and complications were recorded from one week prior until two weeks post index date. Comorbidities were recorded for a 12-month baseline period. Comorbidities of interest were selected based on RSV risk factors and conditions. 2.3 Endpoints Study objectives were to describe the disease and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among older adults in Japan. The baseline characteristics of older adults with RSV in the 12-month pre-event were described to enhance the understanding of the hidden disease burden. During the post-event period, we analyzed the overall incidence of the first RSV episode, the proportion of cases with associated LRTD/URTD, and RSV-related complications. To measure the incremental healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs associated with acute RSV infection, as well as the long-term effects of RSV on HCRU and medical costs, we compared HCRU (mean number of individual outpatient visits and hospitalizations, mean frequency of radiography and oxygen inhalation procedures) and direct medical costs (by age groups [60–74 versus ≥ 75 years], LRTD/URTD, and comorbidities) during three pre-defined timeframes (differences between pre-events and post-events): Period I, 30 days; Period II, 180 days; and Period III, 365 days [15]. 2.4 Statistical Analysis The overall incidence of the first RSV episode was calculated based on the number of cases with at least one RSV event during the study period divided by the sum of person-time at risk, expressed per 1000 person-years with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The MDV cohort was stratified into age groups (60–74 years and ≥ 75 years). Cases were further stratified into LRTD (LRTD ± URTD), URTD (URTD only), and baseline comorbidities (cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic renal failure, and pulmonary conditions) subgroups. Baseline characteristics, clinical outcomes, and duration of hospitalization were analyzed descriptively. The mean numbers of outpatient visits and hospitalizations, as well as medical costs, were compared between the pre-event period (12-month baseline average) and post-event period, the latter including the index date, with an aggregate analysis of the entire study period. Given the large sample size, the use of parametric methods was considered appropriate based on the central limit theorem [16]. Comparisons were analyzed using a paired sample t-test, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. For detailed information regarding the study design, sample size calculation, eligibility criteria, ICD-10 coding algorithms, variables, and data analysis, please see Supplementary Methods. 3 Results 3.1 Baseline Characteristics A total 144 RSV cases were identified in the MDV (60–74 years, n = 77; ≥ 75 years, n = 67) and 34 in the JMDC (60–74 years, n = 34) (Table 1, Supplementary Fig. 1). No RSV case was identified during the 2009–2010 year cycle. The highest count of RSV cases was identified in 2017–2018, with 44 cases (MDV: 38; JMDC: 6). Overall, the number of RSV cases increased over the study period and reached 38 and 36 RSV cases in 2018–2019 and 2019–2020, respectively. The mean (standard deviation, SD) age of the RSV cohorts was 74.5 (9.1) and 64.0 (3.6) years in the MDV and JMDC, respectively (Table 1). Most MDV RSV cases (58%) were treated in large hospitals (> 500 beds). The largest proportion of JMDC RSV cases (47%) were treated in small institutions (0–19 beds) (data not shown). The comorbidity burden, described using the median modified Charlson comorbidity index (mCCI), was 5 and 1 in the MDV and the JMDC cohorts, respectively (Table 1). Comorbidities were defined at baseline assessment and were present in 93–94% of RSV cases, with the most common being type 2 diabetes, followed by heart failure, hypertension, solid tumor malignancies, chronic liver failure, asthma, and COPD. From 2009 to 2019, the overall incidence rate for the MDV RSV cohort was 0.007 per 1000 person-years (95% CI 0.006–0.008). Due to the limited number of RSV cases recorded in the JMDC and the age limitation to 60–74 years, our subsequent analysis focuses on RSV cases recorded in the MDV. For further details about the JMDC cases, please see Supplementary Tables. 3.2 Complications RSV complications were identified from one week prior to and the 2-week period following the date of the first confirmed diagnosis of RSV. Further details are in Supplementary Methods, variables section 6. All RSV cases had LRTD or URTD (or both) associated with their first episode (Table 1). LRTD (with or without URTD) was observed in 78.5% and 58.8% of RSV cases in the MDV and JMDC cohorts, respectively. RSV-related complications were recorded in 61.1% (MDV) and 55.9% (JMDC) (Table 2). Frequent complications included heart failure, pneumonia, bronchitis, and respiratory failure. Exacerbation of asthma, in those with a prior diagnosis of asthma, occurred in 25.0% (MDV) and 20.0% (JMDC). Exacerbation of COPD was recorded in 18.8% of MDV cases with prior COPD, while no cases were recorded in the JMDC cohort. 3.3 Healthcare Resource Utilization Overall, HCRU in the MDV cohort was numerically higher during the post-event period for all timeframes (30, 180, and 365 days) (Fig. 1A, Supplementary Table 1). The average numbers of outpatient visits and hospitalizations per patient were significantly higher within the 30-day post-event period compared with the pre-event period (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event for the average number of outpatient visits was 1.21 [1.50] versus 2.07 [2.30]; for the average number of hospitalizations, it was 0.07 [0.12] versus 0.37 [0.51]; p < 0.001) (Fig. 1A). This impact decreased during the 180- and 365-day post-event periods, with no statistical significance detected in the 365-day post-event period. Similarly, the average number of outpatient visits per JMDC patient increased significantly, by 1.44 in the 30-day post-event period compared with the pre-event period (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event, 2.15 [2.49] versus 3.59 [2.86]; p < 0.001) (Supplementary Table 1). Simple radiography and oxygen inhalation were the two most common treatment procedures, with statistically significant increased use in the MDV cohort post-event across all study periods (Supplementary Table 1). 3.3.1 HCRU by Age Group In the MDV cohort, average outpatient visits and hospitalizations significantly increased post-event in both the 60–74 years (n = 77) and ≥ 75 years (n = 67) age groups (Table 3A). 3.3.2 HCRU by LRTD/URTD Subgroup Among MDV RSV cases with LRTD (n = 113), the average number of outpatient visits per case increased significantly by 0.8 when comparing 30-day periods pre- and post-event (pre-event mean [SD] versus post-event mean [SD]: 1.12 [1.24] versus 1.92 [2.15]; p < 0.001), and the average number of hospitalizations per case also increased significantly, by 0.34 (0.07 [0.10] versus 0.41 [0.53]; p < 0.001). Similarly, among MDV RSV cases with URTD (n = 31), outpatient visits per case increased significantly by 1.07 (1.54 [2.21] versus 2.61 [2.78]; p = 0.048) and hospitalizations per case by 0.14 (0.09 [0.16] versus 0.23 [0.43]; p = 0.039) (Table 3B). 3.3.3 HCRU by Comorbidities For MDV RSV cases with type 2 diabetes (n = 88), pulmonary conditions (n = 52), and cardiovascular conditions (n = 75), the number of outpatient visits per case increased significantly by 0.95 (1.36 [1.55] versus 2.31 [2.65]; p < 0.001), 0.60 (1.15 [0.85] versus 1.75 [1.34]; p < 0.001), and 0.89 (1.40 [1.63] versus 2.29 [2.76]; p = 0.002), respectively, during the first 30 days post-event compared with the pre-event period (Table 3C). The number of hospitalizations per case significantly increased among patients with type 2 diabetes (n = 88) by 0.30 (0.08 [0.13] versus 0.38 [0.53]; p < 0.001), among patients with pulmonary conditions (n = 52) by 0.26 (0.07 [0.12] versus 0.33 [0.47]; p < 0.001), among patients with cardiovascular conditions (n = 75) by 0.39 (0.10 [0.14] versus 0.49 [0.53]; p < 0.001), and among patients with chronic renal failure (n = 23) by 0.28 (0.11 [0.16] versus 0.39 [0.50]; p = 0.010) (Table 3C). 3.4 Cost Analysis In the MDV cohort, average costs in the first 30 days post-event significantly increased by Japanese yen (¥) 196,231.7, compared with the pre-event period (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event costs: ¥132,109.7 [¥230,165.4] versus ¥328,341.4 [¥526,699.1]; p < 0.001), primarily driven by a ¥187,256.0 increase in inpatient hospitalization costs (¥89,544.9 versus ¥276,800.9; p < 0.001 (Fig. 1B, Supplementary Table 2). 3.4.1 Costs by Age Groups In the MDV cohort, elevated HCRU significantly increased costs across age groups. In the 60–74 years group, costs increased by ¥122,552.2 (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event costs: ¥142,653.0 [¥268,553.5] versus ¥265,205.2 [¥515,195.5]; p = 0.012) (Table 3A). For those aged ≥ 75 years, costs increased by ¥280,908.1 (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event costs: ¥119,992.8 [¥177,354.1] versus ¥400,900.9 [¥534,248.5]; p < 0.001), driven by a ¥270,903.9 increase in inpatient costs (¥87,884.1 versus ¥358,788.0; p < 0.001) (Table 3A). 3.4.2 Costs by LRTD/URTD Subgroups For MDV RSV cases with LRTD (n = 113), post-event costs were higher than pre-event by ¥234,250.6 (mean [SD] pre-event versus post-event period: ¥117,484.3 [¥222,607.4] versus ¥351,734.9 [¥562,674.5]; p < 0.001), driven by a significant increase in inpatient costs (¥84,476.6 versus ¥309,533.7; p < 0.001) (Table 3B). Outpatient costs did not significantly increase. For MDV RSV cases with URTD (n = 31), total costs increased by ¥57,646.7 post-event, but this was not statistically significant (Table 3B). 3.4.3 Costs by Comorbidities For MDV RSV cases with chronic renal failure, cardiovascular conditions, type 2 diabetes, or pulmonary conditions, the total medical costs increased by ¥251,060.2, ¥267,994.7, ¥175,618.8, and ¥150,362.9 in the 30 days post-event period, respectively, primarily due to increased inpatient admission costs. Inpatient costs for cardiovascular conditions and type 2 diabetes increased by ¥264,880.7 and ¥171,005.5 (both p < 0.001), respectively. Inpatient costs for chronic renal failure increased by ¥250,977.4 (p = 0.010) (Table 3C). 4 Discussion This is among the first studies describing the clinical and economic burden of RSV infections in older adults in Japan, for 11 yearly cycles from September 2009 to August 2020. The data provided broad population coverage, enabling subpopulation analysis and cross-validation of age-standardized outputs. full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory illness and severe outcomes in older adults. Objective This retrospective cohort study investigated the health and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among adults ≥ 60 years in Japan. Methods Data were collected between 1 September 2008 and 31 August 2021 from the Medical Data Vision (MDV) hospital-based claims database and the insurance-based JMDC database. We investigated RSV-related complications during the first episode. Healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs were compared between baseline (pre-event: 30-day average costs during the 365 days before RSV diagnosis) and post-event (30 days after RSV diagnosis); differences were explored using paired sample t-tests (p < 0.05). Results A total of 178 cases identified between 2009 and 2019 were included in the study, 144 were from the MDV database (mean age 74 years) and 34 from the JMDC database (mean age 64 years). RSV-related complications were recorded in 61.1% and 55.9% of the MDV and JMDC cohorts, respectively. HCRU in the MDV cohort increased significantly from pre- to post-event (average number of outpatient visits per case: 1.21 to 2.07; average number of hospitalizations per case: 0.07 to 0.37), resulting in significant additional medical costs of ¥196,231 (p < 0.001). Conclusions Medically attended RSV infections were associated with substantial short-term increases in HCRU and total medical costs among older adults in Japan. These findings may help inform prevention strategies for severe RSV disease. | Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was associated with substantial short-term increases in healthcare resource utilization and medical costs among medically attended older adults in Japan, particularly during the first 30 days following diagnosis. | | These findings may help inform RSV prevention strategies, including vaccination. | 1 Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common virus affecting individuals of all ages, the most vulnerable being young children and older adults [1]. RSV can lead to severe infections such as pneumonia in older adults, especially those with chronic cardiovascular disease, pulmonary conditions, or diabetes [1,2,3]. Severe RSV infections may require hospitalization or non-invasive ventilation [1]. RSV is associated with lower and upper respiratory tract disease (LRTD/URTD), potentially leading to inflammatory responses that can cause complications such as exacerbation of asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and heart failure [2]. In Japan, the incidence and disease burden of RSV in older adults is likely underestimated due to the lack of routine testing and surveillance. A prospective study estimated that RSV infection occurs in 2.4% of ambulatory older adults in Japan [4]. A recent meta-analysis using 1999–2020 data from high-income countries estimated approximately 700,000 RSV-related acute respiratory infection (ARI) cases, 63,000 hospitalizations, and 4500 in-hospital deaths annually in older adults in Japan [5]. The economic burden of RSV in older adults in Japan is not well documented, but the costs of hospitalization due to RSV contribute considerably to this burden [6]. In 2023, RSV vaccines were approved for individuals aged ≥ 60 years in the USA, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and Japan [7,8,9]. In Japan, the indication was subsequently expanded to include adults aged 50–59 years in 2024 and 18–49 years in 2026, if they were diagnosed with a medical condition that put them at increased risk for severe RSV, such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma.[10]. However, there are currently no specific treatments, highlighting a considerable unmet medical need and the importance of vaccination, especially given the high proportion of Japan’s population that is aged > 65 years (30% in 2022) [11]. Understanding the real-world impact of RSV is essential. Estimating its clinical and economic consequences is key to informing optimal vaccination strategies. We conducted a retrospective analysis using data from two administrative claims databases to explore the disease and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among older adults in Japan. 2 Materials and Methods 2.1 Study Design In this retrospective observational cohort study, we investigated the health and economic burden associated with RSV infection among older adults (≥ 60 years) in Japan from 1 September 2008 to 31 August 2021 (Supplementary Fig. 1). Data from two commercially available administrative databases ensured diverse population coverage: a hospital-based database (Medical Data Vision Co. Ltd. [MDV]; Tokyo, Japan) and an insurance-based database (JMDC Inc. Payer). The MDV is an anonymized health claims database including Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination data covering lump-sum payments for acute-care hospital inpatient costs; as of data analysis, it comprises data for approximately 45 million patients and 35% of the data are from cases aged more than 65 years [12]. The JMDC is an anonymized employer-based health insurance claims database with more than 130 payers, covering inpatient, outpatient, and medication-dispensing services, in addition to annual health-check results; as of data analysis, it stores data of 12 million patients among which 2% are aged 65–74 years [13]. The study complied with all applicable privacy laws. It was out of scope of the Ethical Guidelines for Life Sciences and Medical Research Involving Human Subjects in Japan. We assessed identification periods, which were 1-year cycles (September to August), between 2009 and 2020, accounting for the 12-month baseline and follow-up periods (Supplementary Fig. 1). An index event was defined as the first eligible claim with a diagnostic code for RSV within each 1-year cycle. 2.2 Cases and Case Definitions RSV cases were defined as those having at least one RSV diagnosis claim, based on the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision (ICD-10 codes: B34.8 [RSV infection only], J12.1, J20.5, or J21.0) [6, 14], during the identification period. The first RSV diagnosis within each 1-year cycle was included from the MDV (aged ≥ 60 years) or JMDC (aged 60–74 years) at the time of the index event. Cases with associated LRTD/URTD were defined, based on the relevant ICD-10 codes (URTD: B34.8, J00, J01.0–J01.4, J01.9, J02.0, J02.8–J03.0, J03.8–J04.2, J05.0, J05.1, J06.0, J06.8, J06.9, J30.0–J30.4, J34.0–J34.3, J34.8, J36, J38.0, J38.3, J38.4, J38.7, J39.0–J39.2, J39.8; LRTD: J11.0, J12.0, J12.1, J12.2, J12.3, J12.8, J12.9, J13, J14, J15.0–J16.0, J18.0–J18.2, J18.8, J18.9, J20.0–J21.1, J21.9, J22, J40, J44.0, J44.1, J68.0, J69.0, J69.1, J69.8, J70.2, J98.0, J98.2). The index date for RSV cases was derived using database-specific algorithms incorporating available information such as treatment start or hospital admission dates, claim month/year, and inpatient/outpatient service dates recorded in the same month to estimate the diagnosis date. Prediagnosis healthcare seeking was captured one week prior to the index date, and complications were recorded from one week prior until two weeks post index date. Comorbidities were recorded for a 12-month baseline period. Comorbidities of interest were selected based on RSV risk factors and conditions. 2.3 Endpoints Study objectives were to describe the disease and economic burden of medically attended RSV infections among older adults in Japan. The baseline characteristics of older adults with RSV in the 12-month pre-event were described to enhance the understanding of the hidden disease burden. During the post-event period, we analyzed the overall incidence of the first RSV episode, the proportion of cases with associated LRTD/URTD, and RSV-related complications. title_original: Health and Economic Burden of Severe Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infections Among Older Adults in Japan: A Retrospective Administrative Database Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the health and economic burden of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections in older adults in Japan, as the incidence and disease burden of RSV in this population is likely underestimated due to the lack of routine testing and surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the Medical Data Vision (MDV) hospital-based claims database and the insurance-based JMDC database, covering the period from 1 September 2008 to 31 August 2021. The study included 178 cases of RSV infection, with 144 from the MDV database and 34 from the JMDC database, focusing on adults aged ≥ 60 years.
analysis.methods: Data were collected from two anonymized health claims databases, and comparisons were analyzed using a paired sample t-test with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Healthcare resource utilization (HCRU) and medical costs were compared between pre- and post-event periods.
analysis.main_results: In the MDV cohort, the average number of outpatient visits increased from 1.21 to 2.07, and hospitalizations increased from 0.07 to 0.37 within 30 days post-event, resulting in significant additional medical costs of ¥196,231 (p < 0.001). The impact decreased over time, with no statistical significance detected in the 365-day post-event period. The number of RSV cases increased over the study period, reaching 38 and 36 cases in 2018–2019 and 2019–2020, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the significant health and economic burden of RSV infections in older adults, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions such as vaccination, especially given Japan’s aging population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights into the healthcare resource utilization and costs associated with RSV infections in older adults, supporting the development of strategies for surveillance, prevention, and management in this vulnerable group.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on administrative databases, which may lack detailed clinical information. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential for unmeasured confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study examined the health and economic burden of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections in older adults in Japan using data from two health claims databases. The study found that RSV infections led to a significant increase in healthcare resource utilization and medical costs within 30 days of diagnosis, with the impact diminishing over time. These findings underscore the importance of addressing RSV in older populations, particularly given the high proportion of Japan’s aging population. The study's reliance on administrative data limits its depth, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the observational design and potential for confounding factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估日本老年人严重呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染的健康和经济负担,因为由于缺乏常规检测和监测,该人群的RSV发病率和疾病负担可能被低估。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性队列研究研究使用了来自医疗数据愿景(MDV)医院基于的索赔数据库和基于保险的JMDC数据库的数据,时间范围为2008年9月1日至2021年8月31日。研究包括了178例RSV感染病例,其中144例来自MDV数据库,34例来自JMDC数据库,聚焦于≥60岁的成人。
elements_zh.methods: 数据来自两个匿名的健康索赔数据库,使用配对样本t检验进行分析,统计学显著性设定为p < 0.05。比较了医疗资源利用(HCRU)和医疗费用在事件前和事件后期间的变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 在MDV 队列研究中,事件后30天内门诊就诊次数平均从1.21次增加到2.07次,住院次数从0.07次增加到0.37次,导致显著增加的医疗费用¥196,231(p < 0.001)。随着时间推移,影响逐渐减弱,在事件后365天期间未检测到统计学显著性。RSV病例数量在研究期间有所增加,分别达到2018–2019年的38例和2019–2020年的36例。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为了解RSV感染在老年人中的医疗资源利用和费用提供了关键见解,支持针对监测、预防和管理策略的制定,特别是在这一易感人群中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于其依赖行政数据库,可能缺乏详细的临床信息。由于研究的观察性质和潜在的未测量混杂因素,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估日本老年人严重呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染的健康和经济负担,因为由于缺乏常规检测和监测,该人群的RSV发病率和疾病负担可能被低估。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性队列研究研究使用了来自医疗数据愿景(MDV)医院基于的索赔数据库和基于保险的JMDC数据库的数据,时间范围为2008年9月1日至2021年8月31日。研究包括了178例RSV感染病例,其中144例来自MDV数据库,34例来自JMDC数据库,聚焦于≥60岁的成人。
analysis_zh.methods: 数据来自两个匿名的健康索赔数据库,使用配对样本t检验进行分析,统计学显著性设定为p < 0.05。比较了医疗资源利用(HCRU)和医疗费用在事件前和事件后期间的变化。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在MDV 队列研究中,事件后30天内门诊就诊次数平均从1.21次增加到2.07次,住院次数从0.07次增加到0.37次,导致显著增加的医疗费用¥196,231(p < 0.001)。随着时间推移,影响逐渐减弱,在事件后365天期间未检测到统计学显著性。RSV病例数量在研究期间有所增加,分别达到2018–2019年的38例和2019–2020年的36例。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了RSV感染在老年人中的显著健康和经济负担,强调了需要针对性干预措施如疫苗接种,尤其是在日本老龄化人口的背景下。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究为了解RSV感染在老年人中的医疗资源利用和费用提供了关键见解,支持针对监测、预防和管理策略的制定,特别是在这一易感人群中。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于其依赖行政数据库,可能缺乏详细的临床信息。由于研究的观察性质和潜在的未测量混杂因素,证据强度中等。

full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children is frequently complicated by bacterial co-infection, which significantly aggravates clinical outcomes. The Albumin-to-Alkaline Phosphatase Ratio (AAPR) has recently emerged as a novel immuno-metabolic marker. This study aimed to investigate the association between AAPR and Gram-positive (G + ) versus Gram-negative (G-) bacterial co-infection phenotypes among RSV-infected children, evaluate its discriminative performance, and explore potentially relevant biological pathways. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 153 pediatric patients with laboratory-confirmed RSV and bacterial co-infection. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were employed to determine the independent association and dose-response relationship between AAPR and infection phenotypes. Diagnostic performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Additionally, an exploratory systems biology analysis was performed to identify candidate genes and signaling pathways potentially relevant to the observed association. Results Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that elevated AAPR was independently and inversely associated with the likelihood of G+ infection (OR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15–0.89 for the highest vs. lowest tertile). RCS analysis showed no evidence of a nonlinear association (P for non-linearity = 0.456). The association remained similar after nonlinear adjustment for age and was directionally consistent across age strata; however, it was attenuated after normalization using age-specific pediatric ALP reference limits. AAPR alone showed modest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.599). full_text_sections.full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children is frequently complicated by bacterial co-infection, which significantly aggravates clinical outcomes. The Albumin-to-Alkaline Phosphatase Ratio (AAPR) has recently emerged as a novel immuno-metabolic marker. This study aimed to investigate the association between AAPR and Gram-positive (G + ) versus Gram-negative (G-) bacterial co-infection phenotypes among RSV-infected children, evaluate its discriminative performance, and explore potentially relevant biological pathways. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 153 pediatric patients with laboratory-confirmed RSV and bacterial co-infection. Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses were employed to determine the independent association and dose-response relationship between AAPR and infection phenotypes. Diagnostic performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Additionally, an exploratory systems biology analysis was performed to identify candidate genes and signaling pathways potentially relevant to the observed association. Results Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that elevated AAPR was independently and inversely associated with the likelihood of G+ infection (OR = 0.37; 95% CI: 0.15–0.89 for the highest vs. lowest tertile). RCS analysis showed no evidence of a nonlinear association (P for non-linearity = 0.456). The association remained similar after nonlinear adjustment for age and was directionally consistent across age strata; however, it was attenuated after normalization using age-specific pediatric ALP reference limits. AAPR alone showed modest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.599). Addition of AAPR to CRP, WBC, and NEU increased the AUC from 0.455 to 0.613; however, the difference did not reach the conventional threshold for statistical significance (P = 0.051). Exploratory systems biology analysis identified IL-17-, TNF-, and other inflammation-related pathways as candidates for further investigation. Clinical trial number Not applicable. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between the Albumin-to-Alkaline Phosphatase Ratio (AAPR) and bacterial co-infection phenotypes in children with Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infection. The research highlights the potential of AAPR as an immuno-metabolic marker for distinguishing Gram-positive from Gram-negative bacterial co-infections. Results show an inverse association between elevated AAPR and G+ infection, though this was attenuated after normalization. AAPR demonstrated modest discriminative performance, and its addition to standard markers like CRP, WBC, and NEU slightly improved diagnostic accuracy without reaching statistical significance. The study also identified inflammation-related pathways as candidates for further investigation. However, limitations include the retrospective design and potential bias from de-identified data, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate in strength, with findings grounded in statistical analysis and systems biology approaches.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 儿童 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染经常并发细菌合并感染,这会显着恶化临床结果。本研究旨在调查 RSV 感染儿童中 AAPR 与革兰氏阳性 (G + ) 和革兰氏阴性 (G-) 细菌共感染表型之间的关联,评估其区分性能,并探索潜在的相关生物学途径。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们回顾性分析了 153 名实验室确诊的 RSV 和细菌合并感染的儿童患者。该研究按照赫尔辛基宣言进行,并获得温州医科大学第二附属医院和育英儿童医院伦理委员会批准。
elements_zh.methods: 采用多变量逻辑回归和限制三次样条 (RCS) 分析来确定 AAPR 和感染表型之间的独立关联和剂量反应关系。使用受试者工作特征曲线下面积(AUC)对诊断性能进行量化。进行了探索性系统生物学分析,以确定与观察到的关联可能相关的候选基因和信号通路。
elements_zh.main_results: 多变量逻辑回归表明,升高的 AAPR 与 G+ 感染的可能性独立且呈负相关(OR = 0.37;95% CI:0.15-0.89,最高与 RCS 分析显示没有非线性关联的证据(非线性 P = 0.456)。单独的 AAPR 显示出适度的判别性能(AUC = 0.599)。将 AAPR 添加到 CRP、WBC、 NEU 将 AUC 从 0.455 增加到 0.613;然而,差异并未达到统计学显着性的常规阈值(P = 0.051)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 白蛋白与碱性磷酸酶比率(AAPR)最近成为一种新型免疫代谢标志物。探索性系统生物学分析确定了 IL-17、TNF 和其他炎症相关途径作为进一步研究的候选途径。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发免疫代谢标记物,以早期检测 RSV 感染儿童的细菌合并感染。这些见解可能有助于改进诊断策略和有针对性的治疗方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 使用特定年龄的儿科 ALP 参考限进行标准化后,这种关联性减弱,并且 AUC 的差异未达到统计显着性的常规阈值。该研究是回顾性的,基于未识别的临床数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制普遍性。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 儿童 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染经常并发细菌合并感染,这会显着恶化临床结果。本研究旨在调查 RSV 感染儿童中 AAPR 与革兰氏阳性 (G + ) 和革兰氏阴性 (G-) 细菌共感染表型之间的关联,评估其区分性能,并探索潜在的相关生物学途径。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们回顾性分析了 153 名实验室确诊的 RSV 和细菌合并感染的儿童患者。该研究按照赫尔辛基宣言进行,并获得温州医科大学第二附属医院和育英儿童医院伦理委员会批准。
analysis_zh.methods: 采用多变量逻辑回归和限制三次样条 (RCS) 分析来确定 AAPR 和感染表型之间的独立关联和剂量反应关系。使用受试者工作特征曲线下面积(AUC)对诊断性能进行量化。进行了探索性系统生物学分析,以确定与观察到的关联可能相关的候选基因和信号通路。
analysis_zh.main_results: 多变量逻辑回归表明,升高的 AAPR 与 G+ 感染的可能性独立且呈负相关(OR = 0.37;95% CI:0.15-0.89,最高与 RCS 分析显示没有非线性关联的证据(非线性 P = 0.456)。单独的 AAPR 显示出适度的判别性能(AUC = 0.599)。将 AAPR 添加到 CRP、WBC、 NEU 将 AUC 从 0.455 增加到 0.613;然而,差异并未达到统计学显着性的常规阈值(P = 0.051)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 白蛋白与碱性磷酸酶比率(AAPR)最近成为一种新型免疫代谢标志物。探索性系统生物学分析确定了 IL-17、TNF 和其他炎症相关途径作为进一步研究的候选途径。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于开发免疫代谢标记物,以早期检测 RSV 感染儿童的细菌合并感染。这些见解可能有助于改进诊断策略和有针对性的治疗方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 使用特定年龄的儿科 ALP 参考限进行标准化后,这种关联性减弱,并且 AUC 的差异未达到统计显着性的常规阈值。该研究是回顾性的,基于未识别的临床数据,这可能会引入偏差并限制普遍性。
